subject: Proposal: extended payment window + consolidated quarterly invoicing for Aurelia Labs
messages:
From: Isabella Tran <isabella.tran@aurelia-labs.com>
To: Aditya Rao <aditya_rao@redwood.ai>
Cc: Procurement <procurement@aurelia-labs.com>
Date: Wed, 4 Feb 2026 09:12:00 -0800
Subject: Request: extended payment terms & consolidated quarterly invoicing

Hi Aditya,

Thanks again for the demo yesterday — the team at Aurelia is excited about Redwood's latency and cost profile. We have two procurement constraints that are blocking the PO: 1) our finance org can only process one consolidated invoice per quarter (they require a quarterly invoice schedule rather than monthly), and 2) we need a 90-day payment window (Net-90) tied to our fiscal disbursement cycle.

I attached the SOW and a proposed invoice schedule for your review. Aurelia is willing to sign a two-year commit and can provide an early-payment fee or purchase-order guarantee in exchange for the extended terms, but we need confirmation quickly to align with our Q2 board approval.

Attachments: Aurelia_SOW_v1.pdf (SOW, redlines included), Aurelia_invoice_schedule.xlsx (proposed quarterly invoice dates)

Can Redwood accommodate consolidated quarterly invoicing plus Net-90 if we agree to a 2-year commitment and a 3% early-pay fee? Please advise next steps and who on your side I should loop in for approval.

Best,
Isabella Tran
Head of Procurement, Aurelia Labs

Date: Wed, 4 Feb 2026 13:05:00 -0800
Subject: Re: Request: extended payment terms & consolidated quarterly invoicing

Hi Isabella — really appreciate the clear ask and the SOW. Quick take: we can consider moving to consolidated quarterly invoicing, but Net-90 is outside standard policy for new enterprise deals.

Proposed compromise (what I'd like exec sign-off on):
- Move to quarterly consolidated invoices tied to the dates in your sheet.
- Net-60 standard, but allow Net-90 for one quarter only at contract start as a pilot; thereafter revert to Net-60 unless PO schedule forces Net-90 long term.
- Reduce price by 3% (early-pay fee equivalent) in exchange for a 2-year commit and an irrevocable PO.
- Require purchase order number on each invoice and ACH or wire as the payment method once PO is issued.

This mitigates cash exposure while giving Aurelia the operational cadence you need. I'll need exec approval for the extended Net-90 pilot and the concession on payment terms. Marissa / Sean / Karthik — can you weigh in on risk and approval? If approved, I suggest Legal add a clause limiting Net-90 to the first quarter unless finance signs off to extend.

Thanks,
Aditya
Enterprise Sales, Redwood Inference
aditya_rao@redwood.ai

Subject: Fwd: Request: extended payment terms & consolidated quarterly invoicing — internal analysis

Team — forwarding Aurelia's request and Aditya's proposed compromise. Quick internal analysis:

1) ARR / cash impact:
- ACV for the 2-year commit would be $480k (annualized). With a 3% concession that's ~$14.4k revenue concession per year.
- Switching to quarterly invoices delays cash collection by ~30-60 days on average compared to monthly, plus the Net-90 pilot increases DSO exposure for Q1.

2) Risk factors:
- Counterparty: Aurelia is venture-backed, Series C, positive liquidity signals but procurement insists on quarterly cycles.
- PO guarantees: if we require an irrevocable PO and include an early-pay fee structure, we reduce credit risk.
- Legal: need a contract clause that limits Net-90 to the initial quarter and puts automatic revert to Net-60 unless Finance signs an extension.

3) Recommendation (low friction):
- Approve the quarterly invoicing and a Net-90 pilot for the first invoice only, conditioned on:
  a) Signed 2-year commit (minimum revenue guarantee),
  b) Irrevocable PO tied to each quarterly invoice,
  c) 3% discount for the term,
  d) Auto-debit/ACH preferred as fallback, and
  e) Legal to insert Net-90 cap (pilot scope) + termination language in case of missed payments.

If you want to be more conservative: require Net-60 with a one-time grace to align to their fiscal calendar; hold the 3% concession until we receive the first PO.

Please advise — Aditya needs to respond to Isabella by EOD tomorrow to keep their procurement timeline.

— Marissa
Director, Deal Desk | Redwood Inference
marissa_cole@redwood.ai

Attachments: (copied) Aurelia_SOW_v1.pdf, Aurelia_invoice_schedule.xlsx

From: Sean Gallagher <sean_gallagher@redwood.ai>
To: Aditya Rao <aditya_rao@redwood.ai>, Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.ai>, Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.ai>, Isabella Tran <isabella.tran@aurelia-labs.com>
Date: Thu, 5 Feb 2026 15:47:00 -0800
Subject: Re: Request: extended payment terms & consolidated quarterly invoicing — decision

Thanks for the analysis, Marissa, and thanks Aditya for the proposed compromise. After reviewing the numbers and Aurelia's profile I'm comfortable approving with the following firm conditions: 

1) Approve: consolidated quarterly invoicing + a one-time Net-90 for the first quarter only (pilot). Subsequent invoices revert to Net-60 unless Finance signs an extension in writing.
2) Approve: 3% price concession for the two-year commit, contingent on receipt of an irrevocable PO before the first invoice is issued.
3) Require: Legal to add explicit language limiting Net-90 to the initial invoice and adding a cure period (15 days) for late payment before termination rights kick in.
4) Require: Finance to add an ACH fallback clause and credit review hold for any invoice that ages beyond 75 days.

Aditya — you have approval to confirm to Isabella under those conditions. Please copy legal (karthik_iyer) on the signature page and add the PO upload requirement in the SOW. If Aurelia pushes for Net-90 beyond Q1, escalate back to me with updated credit checks and a revised risk memo.

Approved — Sean Gallagher
